content.text: Section 11 is a full transition regime; no redline needed.

input.quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
input.rationale: Section 11 satisfies the preferred position on its material terms. § 11.1 applies "Upon expiry or termination for any reason" and gives up to six months of transition assistance (knowledge transfer, export support, migration, cooperation with a replacement supplier, continued service at the same scope and service levels). Pricing is fixed at "the rates in the expiring Order Form", which is at least as favourable to us as the preferred "then-current rates" because it removes exposure to a price uplift, so it is not a deviation. § 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a "complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format" with relationships and metadata, and expressly bars withholding data over a fee dispute; the thirty-day clock runs from our own request, a trigger we control, so post-termination return is assured. § 11.3 requires secure deletion from active systems and backups after we confirm successful return, with written certification by an authorized officer, and confines any law-required retained copy to protected, non-use status — i.e. certified deletion occurs after return, as preferred. § 16.5 confirms Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15, so no other clause cuts across this. No walk-away features (no immediate deletion, no denial of return) appear anywhere in the document.
